recap.back_html: CSV: text, no types. Parquet: columnar, typed, compressed. Delta: Parquet files plus a transaction log with versions.
Lake: files, structure on read. Warehouse: typed tables for SQL. Lakehouse: open tables in a lake, read by Spark and SQL.
Load raw first, transform inside the platform: bronze (as received), silver (clean), gold (aggregated).
OneLake is the one lake (GA). Lakehouse tables are Delta (GA). The SQL analytics endpoint queries them with T-SQL (GA).

lessons.takeaway_html: Keep data once, in a typed table format such as Delta, and let each engine read it, instead of exporting copies to untyped files.
lessons.title: Data platform vocabulary, files, tables, lakes and warehouses

recap.back_html: Data sits in source tables. The model describes tables, relationships and measures. Reports hold visuals that query the model.
A column is worked out per row and stored. A measure is worked out when a visual asks, in that visual's filter context.
A measure dividing totals: DIVIDE ( SUM ( reach ), SUM ( base ) ). Never average per-row percentages.
Import copies and refreshes. DirectQuery queries the source each time. Direct Lake (GA) reads OneLake Delta tables directly.

snippets: Weighted reach % = DIVIDE ( SUM ( fact[reach] ), SUM ( fact[base] ) )
lessons.takeaway_html: Put ratios in measures that divide totals, and let filter context decide what each total covers.
